docs.title: New Character Creation Content
docs.text:
1.0.0

This documentation brings together the character creation options added for the Spark of Madness campaign.

docs.title: Ancient Displacer Beast
docs.text:
An old Displacer Beast hardened by the years. The worse decision you can make is to attack his younger kinds, because it will protect them at all cost.

Armor Class 14 (natural armor) \ Hit Points 106 (12d10+40) \ Speed 40ft.

STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 20 (+5) 14 (+2) 16 (+3) 8 (-1) 16 (+3) 10 (+0)

Senses darkvision 60ft., stealh +3, acrobatic +4, athletism +2, passive perception 13\ Languages --\ Challenge 4 (1200xp)

Avoidance : If the displacer beast is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

Mirror Illusion : The displacer beast projects a magical illusion that makes it appear to be standing near its actual location, causing attack rolls against it to have disadvantage. If it is hit by an attack, this trait is disrupted until the end of its next turn. This trait is also disrupted while the displacer beast is incapacitated or has a speed of 0.

Actions

Psychic Tentacles : Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage + 14 (4d6) psychic damage. On a hit, the target must succeed a wisdow saving throw DC 12 or getting frightened until the end of his next turn.

Bonus Actions

Protective Displacement : The displacer beast teleport itself and one optional ally in 10ft from it at a visible location in 40ft from it. The beast and the ally gain 2d4 temporary hit points.\ An illusion of the beast stay at the start location and can make opportunity attacks. The illusion disapear at the start of the next beast's turn.

docs.title: Displacer Beast
docs.text:
This monstrous predator takes its name from its ability to mask itself with illusion, displacing light so that it appears to be somewhere it is not.

Armor Class 13 (natural armor) \ Hit Points 85 (10d10+30) \ Speed 40ft.

STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 18 (+4) 16 (+3) 16 (+3) 6 (-2) 12 (+1) 8 (-1)

Senses darkvision 60ft., stealh +5, acrobatic +4, passive perception 11\ Languages --\ Challenge 3 (700xp)

Avoidance : If the displacer beast is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

Mirror Illusion : The displacer beast projects a magical illusion that makes it appear to be standing near its actual location, causing attack rolls against it to have disadvantage. If it is hit by an attack, this trait is disrupted until the end of its next turn. This trait is also disrupted while the displacer beast is incapacitated or has a speed of 0.

Actions

Multiattack : The displacer beast makes two attacks with its tentacles.

Tentacle : Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage + 3 (1d6) piercing damage.

Bonus Actions

Displacement : The displacer beast teleport itself and one optional target in 5ft from it at a visible location in 30ft from it. The target takes 2d4 psychic damage.\ An illusion of the beast stay at the start location and can make opportunity attacks. The illusion disapear at the start of the next beast's turn.

docs.title: Displacer Cub
docs.text:
Smaller and weaker form of a Displacer Beast. If you see one, an adult see you too.

Armor Class 11 (natural armor) \ Hit Points 34 (4d10+12) \ Speed 30ft.

STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 14 (+2) 12 (+1) 12 (+1) 4 (-3) 10 (+0) 4 (-3)

Senses darkvision 60ft., stealth +8, acrobatic +2, passive perception 10\ Languages --\ Challenge 1 (200xp)

Avoidance : If the displacer cub is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

Actions

Multiattack : The cub makes two attacks : one with its bite, and one with both his tentacles.

Bite : Melee Weapon Attack : +4 to hit, reach 5ft., one target. Hit 4 (1d4+2) piercing damages.

Tentacles : Melee Weapon Attack : +4 to hit, reach 5ft., one target. Hit 9 (2d4+4) bludgeoning damage.

First Illusion : As an action, the cub can summon an illusion of itself in a 60ft range. When creating this illusion, it can define movements the illusion will do (lick it's paw, run in circle, sleep...). It can also use Meow from his illusion.

Bonus Actions

Meow : The cub can meow, and all enemies in a 30ft range from it :\ In combat : must succeed a wisdom saving throw DC 12 or the next attack roll or DC targeting them benefits from +5.\ Outside combat : should investigate the noise.

docs.title: Mythic Displacer Beast
docs.text:
This terrifying predator is an old Displacer Beast, larger than his kinds. His illusions and brute force are a nightmare for the unfortunate souls who find themselves chosen as his prey.

Armor Class 15 (natural armor) \ Hit Points 137 (14d10+60) \ Speed 40ft.

STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 22 (+6) 14 (+2) 18 (+4) 10 (+0) 14 (+2) 12 (+1)

Senses darkvision 60ft., acrobatic +4, athletism +4, passive perception 13\ Languages Elvish Sylvan\ Challenge 6 (2500xp)

Avoidance : If the displacer beast is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

Mirror Illusion : The displacer beast projects a magical illusion that makes it appear to be standing near its actual location, causing attack rolls against it to have disadvantage. If it is hit by an attack, this trait is disrupted until the end of its next turn. This trait is also disrupted while the displacer beast is incapacitated or has a speed of 0.

Actions

Multiattack : The displacer beast makes three attacks, one bite and two with its tentacles.

Bite : Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage. On a hit, the target must succeed a wisdow saving throw DC 16 or start bleeding.

Tentacle : Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (4d6 + 8) bludgeoning damage + 14 (4d6) piercing damage.

Bonus Actions

Greater Displacement : The displacer beast teleport itself and one optional target in 10ft from it at a visible location in 60ft from it. The target takes 2d8 psychic damage.\ An illusion of the beast stay at the start location and can make opportunity attacks. The illusion disapear at the start of the next beast's turn.

Illusory Duplication : The displacer beast create an Illusion copy of itself. This copy can attacks and make opportunity attacks, replacing damages by psychic damages. It has 1 hit point and an AC of 13.

docs.title: Young Displacer Beast
docs.text:
Not yet as strong as an adult Displacer Beast, but can be dangerous for those who underestimate it.

Armor Class 12 (natural armor) \ Hit Points 55 (6d10+22) \ Speed 35ft.

STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA 16 (+3) 16 (+3) 14 (+2) 6 (-2) 12 (+1) 6 (-2)

Senses darkvision 60ft., stealh +7, acrobatic +6, passive perception 11\ Languages --\ Challenge 2 (450xp)

Avoidance : If the displacer beast is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

Actions

Multiattack : The displacer beast makes two attacks with its tentacles.

Tentacle : Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) bludgeoning damage + 2 (1d4) piercing damage.

Bonus Actions

Basic Displacement : The displacer beast teleport itself at a visible location in 30ft from it. After the teleportation, the beast is hidden.\ An illusion of the beast stay at the start location and can make opportunity attacks. The illusion disapear at the start of the next beast's turn.

docs.title: Sandstorm
docs.text: When caught in a sandstorm, your vision is reduced to 15 feet, and you must regularly succeed on a DC 8 Constitution saving throw or be blinded.

docs.title: Weapon : Bladed Buckler
docs.text:
A small shield attached to the forearm. The front of the shield joins into a wide, sharp blade.

Cost : 12 gp Damage : 1d6 slashing Weight : 5 lb Properties : Light, Finesse, +1 AC

Although this weapon doesn't need to be held in your hand, it hinders you if you try to use a weapon in that hand. If you do so, the weapon in that hand doesn't benefit from your proficiency bonus.

This weapon counts as both a weapon and a shield.

docs.title: Feats
docs.text: No character creation feats have been added yet. This section will be updated if new feats are introduced for the campaign.

docs.title: Kensut
docs.text:
These humanoid foxes originate from the south of Faerûn and have long been outcasts. Most often working as merchants or highwaymen, they are particularly at home in desert regions. Long ago, one of them became wealthy enough to construct a great vessel, allowing him to migrate to the nearby island of Samargol, taking as many of his kin along with him as possible.

  • Ability Score Increase : When determining your character’s ability scores, increase one score by 2 and increase a different score by 1, or increase three different scores by 1. You can't raise any of your scores above 20.

  • Age : Kensuts have lifespans equivalent to humans.

  • Alignment : Kensuts tend toward chaotic alignments, as impulse and fancy guide their decisions. They are often nomads who live by commerce or become highwaymen.

  • Size : You are Medium or Small. You choose the size when you select this race.

  • Speed : Your walking speed is 30 feet, and you have a climbing speed of 20 feet.

  • Fox Cunning : You have proficiency in Deception and Stealth skills. When rolling a Deception check, add your intelligence modifier (minimum 0) to the roll.

  • Desert Wanderer : You have been accustomed to deserts and sandstorms since childhood. While in a sandstorm, you have advantage on saving throws against its effects and can see through it to a distance of 30 feet. You also don't suffer adverse effects from high temperatures in the desert.

  • Languages : Your character can speak, read, and write Common and one other language that you and your DM agree is appropriate for the character. The Player’s Handbook offers a list of languages to choose from. The DM is free to modify that list for a campaign.

docs.title: Fighter: Revised Arcane Archer
docs.text: An Arcane Archer studies a unique elven method of archery that weaves magic into attacks to produce supernatural effects. Arcane Archers are some of their most elite warriors among the elves. They stand watch over the fringes of elven domains, keeping a keen eye out for trespassers and using magic-infused arrows to defeat monsters and invaders before they can reach elven settlements. Over the centuries, the methods of these elf archers have been learned by members of other races who can also balance arcane aptitude with archery.

docs.title: Arrow Conjuration
docs.text: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to conjure arrows when you draw your bow or crossbow (or a dart or bullet just before firing). The conjured projectile disappears after hitting or missing a target.

docs.title: Arcanic points
docs.text: At 3rd level, you have 4 Arcanic points, and you gain 1 more whenever you gain a fighter level. You can spend these points to add cumulative effects to a shot before firing. The maximum number of Arcanic points you can spend on one shot equals your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. If the shot misses, you regain half the expended points, rounded up. You regain all expended Arcanic points after a long rest.

docs.title: Arcane shots
docs.text:
At 3rd level, when using Arrow Conjuration, you can imbue the projectile with magic. Choose 3 options in the table below.

Option Effect Arcanic cost Seeking Arrow Choose a target you can see. You don'thave to make an attack roll. The arrow follows the rules of magic missile. 2 Omniscient Arrow Choose a target you have seen within the past minute. You don't have to make an attack roll. The arrow follows the rules of magic missile. 3 Faerie Arrow Creatures hit by this arrow are affected by faerie fire until the end of their next turn. 1 Mitotic Arrow The arrow duplicates in flight. For each duplicate, you choose a target or location within a 45-degree cone from you. This limitation doesn't apply if you also add the Seeking or Omniscient effect. 1 per duplicate Banishing Arrow You use abjuration magic to try to temporarily banish the target to a harmless location in the Feywild. The creature hit by the arrow must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be banished. While banished, its speed is 0 and it is incapacitated. At the end of its next turn, the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space. 3 Elementary Arrow You load the arrow with elemental energy. Choose fire, cold, lightning, acid, or poison. The arrow deals bonus damage equal to 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier damage of the chosen type. 1 Explosive Arrow The arrow explodes on impact. If it directly hits a target, that target takes the arrow's damage. Each creature in the explosion must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking the arrow's effects plus 1d8 + Arcanic points expended force damage on a failed save. 1 for 5 feet, 3 for 10 feet, 7 for 15 feet Radiant Arrow The arrow emits bright magical light. It dismisses magical darkness along its path and at its destination. The arrow deals 1d8 radiant damage. Each creature hit must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become blinded until the end of its next turn. 2 Putrefaction Arrow The arrow is filled with death energy. It deals 1d8 necrotic damage, doubled against plants. A creature hit can't be healed until the end of its next turn. 1

The saving throw DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.

docs.title: Curving Shot
docs.text: At 7th level, you learn how to direct an errant arrow toward a new target. When you make an attack roll with a magic arrow and miss, you can use a bonus action to reroll the attack roll against a different target within 60 feet of the original target. You also choose one additional Arcane Shot option, and effects dealing damage are improved to 2d8.

docs.title: Counter shot
docs.text: At 10th level, you can use your reaction and 1 Arcane point to shoot a special arrow at another projectile, whether it is magical or not, and destroy it. To do so, you must make an attack roll with a result equal higher than the other projectile's attack roll or its spell save DC + 2 per spell level. You also choose one additional Arcane Shot option.

docs.title: Returning magic
docs.text: At 15th level, when you miss an attack with an Arcane Shot, you regain all Arcanic points spent for that attack. You also choose one additional Arcane Shot option, and effects dealing damage are improved to 3d8.

docs.title: Spectral Archer
docs.text: At 18th level, you can shoot an arrow from any point within 30 feet of you. A spectral archer appears, fires the arrow, and then vanishes. You also choose one additional Arcane Shot option, and effects dealing damage are improved to 4d8.

docs.title: Rogue : Card Bettor
docs.text: Legend has it that the first "Card Bettor" was an assassin so gifted that every contract he took on bored him. One evening, while drinking and playing cards with a magician friend, the two came up with a brilliant idea. This combat method did not meet with much success, as the assassin died during his very next contract, having drawn the wrong card. Nevertheless, those who still practice it have sown panic among a group of mentalist bandits.

docs.title: Cards Conjuration
docs.text: You have proficiency with card games. At 3rd level, you learn to create magical duplicates from cards. You must have the original card on you to duplicate it. If it's an Arcanic card, it must be part of your deck. You can throw those duplicates, using your Dexterity modifier for the attack roll and dealing 1d6 slashing damage (without adding your Dexterity modifier). The conjuration can be part of a ranged weapon attack.

docs.title: Arcanic Card Deck
docs.text:
At 3rd level, you learn to identify if a card is magical or not. During a 1-hour ritual, you can imbue your mind with exactly six different Arcanic cards. You also assign one number from 1 to 6 to each card. Arcanic cards deal bonus damage and can have an amplified effect.

When you hit with an Arcanic card, you announce a number between 1 and 6. The first damage roll (1d6 slashing damage) determines the thrown card (by its assigned number). If it matches the announced number, it triggers the amplified effect. If you hit with your Sneak Attack, double the bonus damage from the Arcanic card. You start with 6 of these cards in your inventory :

Card Bonus Damages Amplified Effect The bard 1d6 psychic damage Charisma saving throw: disadvantage on the next attack roll The cleric 1d6 healing Constitution saving throw: healing the target receives is replaced by an equivalent amount of necrotic damage until the end of its next turn The fighter 1d6 slashing damage Strength saving throw: can't make multiple attacks until the end of its next turn The paladin 1d6 radiant damage Wisdom saving throw: blinded until the end of its next turn The barbarian 1d6 bludgeoning damage Wisdom saving throw: frightened until the end of its next turn The druid 1d6 poison damage Dexterity saving throw: restrained until the end of its next turn The monk 1d6 thunder damage You can make another attack The rogue 1d6 necrotic damage Constitution saving throw: bleeding until the end of its next turn The ranger 1d6 piercing damage Intelligence saving throw: silenced for 1 turn and concentration is broken The warlock 1d6 force damage Charisma saving throw: take 1d6 force damage and are pushed 10 feet away The wizard 1d6 fire, cold, lightning, or poison damage Double the damage The sorcerer 1d6 fire damage It explodes in a 10-foot radius. Creatures in the area make a Dexterity saving throw and take 1d6 fire damage The artificer 1d6 acid damage Dexterity saving throw: -2 AC until the end of its next turn

The Arcanic cards DC use your intelligence modifier.

docs.title: Fast draw
docs.text: At 9th level, when you use your action to throw a card, you can throw two cards at two different targets using the same attack roll.

docs.title: Stacked deck
docs.text: At 13th level, you add one additional d6 to the damage of each Arcanic card. Moreover, once per short rest, you can choose the result of a card's damage roll.

docs.title: Very fast draw
docs.text: At 17th level, Fast Draw can throw a card at a third target.

docs.title: Druid : Circle of the Displacer
docs.text: Druids of the Circle of the Displacer are as rare as the beasts they admire—and just as formidable.

docs.title: Hunter Wild Shape
docs.text: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you gain the ability to use Wild Shape on your turn as a bonus action, rather than as an action. Additionally, while you are transformed by Displacer Shapes, you add the beast's Dexterity modifier to its AC.

docs.title: Displacer Shapes
docs.text:
At 2nd level, using Wild Shape, you gain the ability to transform into a displacer beast. At higher levels, you unlock more powerful shapes.

Level Required Shape 2 Displacer Cub 6 Young Displacer Beast 10 Displacer Beast 14 Ancient Displacer Beast 18 Mythic Displacer Beast

At 18th level, while you are transformed by Displacer Shapes, you can only cast illusion spells with Beast Spells feature.

docs.title: A Trail of Fear
docs.text: At 6th level, you are accustomed to nature and hunting. You gain proficiency in Survival (or expertise if you are already proficient), and you can smell the exact direction of a creature you have frightened during the last 24 hours, up to 1000 feet.

docs.title: Mental Crack
docs.text: At 10th level, your psychic damage ignores resistance. Moreover, while you are hidden from a target, you double your proficiency bonus when determining the DC of your spells that require a Wisdom saving throw.

docs.title: Displacer friend
docs.text: At 14th level, displacer beasts become friendly toward you, and you gain the ability to communicate with them. Moreover, you can cast the Displacement feature as a 2nd-level spell. For each level of upcasting, the feature deals an additional 2d4 psychic damage.

docs.title: Druid : Circle of the Cauldron
docs.text: These druids are rarely found together, as they more or less detest one another—a sentiment stemming from an ancient rite that involved presenting one’s latest alchemical inventions to the rest of the group, and the last iteration of this event proved to be explosive. Druids from other circles mock them, claiming that the members of the Circle of the Cauldron had a falling out over a cooking contest.

docs.title: Circle Spells
docs.text:
When you join this circle at 2nd level, you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of the Cauldron Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the Druid Spell List, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

Druid Level Spells 2nd Catapult, Tasha's Caustic Brew 3rd Barkskin, Alter Self 5th Plant Growth, Gaseous Form 7th Polymorph, Sickening Radiance 9th Immolation, Contagion

docs.title: Alchemy
docs.text:
At 2nd level, you learn to create brews from plants you magically grow. You know a number of recipes equal to half your druid level. Whenever you gain a level in this class and don't learn a new recipe, you can replace one recipe you know with another one.

Recipe Druid Level Required Usage Effect Healing Elixir 2nd Drink A creature that drinks this elixir regains 2d4 + your Wisdom modifier hit points. Charming Perfume 2nd Spread You apply the perfume to one creature. For 10 minutes, any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of the perfumed creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become charmed by the perfumed creature until the start of its next turn. Sticky Mixture 2nd Area When the flask breaks, it covers a 20-foot-radius area with a sticky substance that creates difficult terrain. Explosive Oil 2nd Area When the flask breaks, it covers the ground in a 10-foot-radius area with an explosive mixture. If the surface takes any fire damage, it explodes. Each creature in the explosion must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d4 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Smoke Bomb 2nd Area When the flask breaks, it creates a cloud of smoke in a 10-foot radius. The smoke blocks line of sight, and each creature in the area is blinded while there. The smoke lasts for 1 minute. Tempest in a Bottle 2nd Area When the flask breaks, it releases a burst of wind in a 5-foot radius. Each creature in the area must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet away from the center of the blast. Restorative Potion 6th Drink A creature that drinks this potion gains the benefits of the lesser restoration spell. Gnar's Wrath 6th Drink A creature that drinks this potion transforms into a Huge beast for 1 minute. Its size increases by one category, it gains claws that deal 1d4 + its Strength modifier slashing damage (unarmed strike), and its Strength modifier increases by your Wisdom modifier. It can make an unarmed strike as a bonus action. When the effect ends, the creature gains one level of exhaustion. Auril's Grasp 6th Spread A creature affected by the potion must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become restrained by ice. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the beginning of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Hiatea's Embrace 6th Spread A creature affected by the potion is encased in an icy cocoon and gains resistance to all damage. The cocoon grants the creature temporary hit points equal to 1d4 × (your Wisdom modifier + 1). While the cocoon lasts, the creature regains 2d4 hit points at the end of each of its turns. The effect lasts for up to 1 minute. The creature can leave the cocoon by using a bonus action. Bomb 6th Area When the flask breaks, it explodes in a 5-foot radius. Each creature in the explosion must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 1d4 force + 2d4 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Talona's Gas 6th Area When the flask breaks, it unleashes a greenish cloud in a 5-foot radius. Each creature in the cloud or that ends its turn there must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d4 poison damage and becoming poisoned until the end of its next turn on a failed save, or taking half as much damage on a successful one. Dryad's Kiss 14th Spread A creature hit by the flask must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become Petrified until the end of its next turn and gain vulnerability to fire damage for the duration. Nala's Bubbles 14th Area When the flask breaks, it unleashes a cloud of small bubbles in a 20-foot radius. The entire area is treated as underwater, except for the purposes of movement, and is difficult terrain. Smell of Madness 14th Area When the flask breaks, it creates a cloud of purple smoke in a 10-foot radius that lasts for 3 rounds. A creature that can breathe and starts its turn in the cloud must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or regard every other creature as hostile until the start of its next turn. Infernal Megabomb 14th Area When the flask breaks, it explodes in a 10-foot radius. Each creature in the explosion must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d4 force + 3d4 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

You can carry a number of potions equal to your druid level + your Wisdom modifier. During a long rest, you can replenish your supply of potions if you have access to soil in which to grow the plants. You choose any combination of potions to carry. Each 14th-level potion requires a spell slot of 1st level or higher to create, and a higher-level spell slot allows you to create more of them.

The saving throw DC for your potions equals your spell save DC.

A creature hit by a thrown potion takes 1 bludgeoning damage.

docs.title: Humanoid Artillery
docs.text:
At 6th level, you become better at throwing potions. When you make an attack roll to throw one of your flasks, you add your Wisdom modifier to the roll.

In addition, you can throw a flask and cast a spell as part of the same action, provided the spell's level is one lower than the level of your highest-level spell slot.

docs.title: Empowered Brewings
docs.text: At 10th level, your potions use d8s instead of d4s.

docs.title: Secret Ingredient
docs.text: At 14th level, a creature that makes a saving throw as a result of one of your potions has disadvantage on that saving throw. In addition, you automatically succeed on saving throws you make as a result of your own potions.

docs.title: Paladin : Oath of Splendor
docs.text: The Oath of Splendor belongs to paladins who seek absolute perfection in both their might and their elegance. To them, every battle is a work of art in which mastery, grace, and brutality must harmonize perfectly. Through their enchanted armor, they can assume various forms of power, borrowing the attributes of the greatest creatures and supernatural forces. Unwavering in the face of adversity, these paladins refuse defeat, continuing to fight even when their bodies ought to give out.

docs.title: Tenets of Splendor
docs.text: Though the exact words and strictures of the Oath of Splendor vary, paladins of this oath share these tenets. - The pursuit of perfection. You can always do better, and you always strive to do so. - Never give up. You never accept defeat in a serious fight. - Elegance in violence. A fight is an artistic performance. Brute force without mastery is merely vulgarity, and victory is as important as the manner in which it is achieved.

docs.title: Oath Spells
docs.text: Paladin level Spells 3rd Zephyr Strike, Heroism 5th Cloud of Daggers, Warding Wind 9th Wind Wall, Intellect Fortress 13th Death Ward, Freedom of Movement 17th Steel Wind Strike, Far Step

docs.title: Channel Divinity
docs.text:
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

Wardrobe of Splendor. As a bonus action, you can expend your Channel Divinity to imbue your armor with a blessing. For 1 minute, when you use this Channel Divinity or as a bonus action while it lasts, you can choose one of the blessings in the table below. The blessing ends any spell affecting the armor and prevents any spell from affecting it, except for spells granted by a blessing.

Armor blessing Effects Angel of steel armor You gain a flying speed of 30 feet. When a creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to cast the sword burst cantrip. Devil of steel armor You gain a flying speed of 30 feet. When your melee attack reduces a creature to hit points equal to or lower than your Charisma modifier, it dies. When you kill a creature, each other non-ally creature within 15 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you until the end of its next turn. Armor of the Flame Empress You have resistance to fire damage. The first melee attack you make on each of your turns benefits from the green-flame blade cantrip. Armor of the Lightning Empress You have resistance to lightning damage. When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a casting of lightning lure. Armor of the Frozen Golem You have resistance to cold damage. At the beginning of your turn, ice forms around your armor, granting you temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier until the start of your next turn. Armor of the Sea King You have resistance to acid damage and a swimming speed of 30 feet. When a creature hits you, you can use your reaction to cast acid splash at that creature. Armor of the Cloud Giant You can't be moved against your will, and difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement. Your Strength modifier increases by your Charisma modifier. Mithril rampart You gain the benefits of blade ward. Your body can protect other creatures from directional area effects, such as fireball and lightning bolt. Clear Heart You lose the bonus to Armor Class granted by your armor, but you add that amount to any ability check or saving throw you make using Dexterity or Wisdom. Armor of Feline Rush Your walking speed increases by 20 feet, and moving doesn't provoke opportunity attacks. Robe of the Archfey You can cast misty step by expending a spell slot. You are immune to the charmed condition. Whenever a creature deals damage to you, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is charmed by you until the start of your next turn. Armor of the Morning Star You have resistance to radiant damage, and your armor sheds light as if affected by the light spell. Your melee attacks can become ranged attacks with a range of 30 feet, using Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls, and deal radiant damage, as you throw waves of light with your blade. Armor of the Destiny You have advantage on saving throws against spells. The first time on each of your turns that you hit a creature with a melee attack, you break its concentration, and it is silenced until the end of its next turn.

The blessing can change the armor's appearance, but it doesn't fool someone trying to determine whether you are wearing armor.

You can end this effect on your turn (no action required). When the effect ends, your armor returns to its original state.

Inspiring Speech. You can make a short monologue or song, your words clinging to the mind of one creature of your choice that can hear you, to help it approach perfection. As an action, you make a Performance check. The creature can add half the result to any ability check it makes for 1 minute or until it fails an ability check.

docs.title: Aura of Perfection
docs.text: Starting at 7th level, whenever you or an ally within 10 feet of you hits with an attack roll, the attack deals extra damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1). The extra damage is of the same type as the attack. You must be conscious to grant this bonus. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

docs.title: Too Formidable
docs.text:
Beginning at 15th level, when you would make a death saving throw, you can instead rise one last time with 1 hit point. Until the end of your next turn, your speed is doubled, you can't be restrained, you ignore the effects of exhaustion, you are immune to all damage, and all your attacks are critical hits. When the effect ends, you gain 3 levels of exhaustion.

Does this woman feel no pain at all? Does she feel no fear?

docs.title: Perfected Armor
docs.text:
At 20th level, each of your Wardrobe of Splendor blessings grants you access to a specific spell. You can cast one of these spells once without expending a spell slot.

Armor Spell Angel of steel armor conjure volley - works with a magic weapon, and your weapon reappears in your hand Devil of steel armor enervation - the reactivation can be used as a multiattack Armor of the Flame Empress Immolation Armor of the Lightning Empress Destructive Wave Armor of the Frozen Golem Cone of Cold Armor of the Sea King Maelstrom Armor of the Cloud Giant Bigby's Hand Mithril rampart Wall of Force Clear Heart Synaptic Static Armor of Feline Rush Steel Wind Strike Robe of the Archfey Dominate Person Armor of the Morning Star Holy Weapon Armor of the Destiny Mislead

docs.title: Barbarian : path of the anvil
docs.text: Barbarians who follow the Path of the Anvil temper their fury like iron in a forge. Their rage kindles a searing inner heat, turning each blow into a hammer strike and making them stubborn defenders who grow more dangerous the longer a battle rages.

docs.title: Armored Defense (Replaces Unarmored Defense)
docs.text: At 3rd level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools. While raging, you add your Constitution modifier to your AC and have advantage on Constitution saving throws.

docs.title: Molten fist
docs.text: At 3rd level, while raging, your melee attacks deal extra fire damage equal to your Constitution modifier.

docs.title: Burning rage
docs.text: At 6th level, while raging, you have resistance to fire damage. As a bonus action, you can unleash a burst of flames. Each creature within 5 feet of you takes 1d4 + your Constitution modifier fire damage.

docs.title: Erratic flames
docs.text: At 10th level, Burning Rage frees you from the restrained and grappled conditions. Additionally, when you use a bonus action to end your rage, you can release your inner fire. Each creature (except yourself) in a 10-foot-radius burst takes a number of d10s of fire damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

docs.title: Wrath of the forge
docs.text: At 14th level, while raging, when an enemy hits you with a melee attack, it takes 2d4 + your Constitution modifier fire damage. Moreover, Molten Fist and Burning Rage deal one additional d4 fire damage.

docs.title: Bard : School of the Cascade
docs.text: The magic of the bards of the School of the Cascade manifests as sparkling, pure water that leaps from creature to creature, healing wounds and easing torments.

docs.title: Revitalizing Water
docs.text: At 3rd level, when you restore hit points, the healing manifests as flying water orbs. As an action, you can conjure up to 1 liter of water.

docs.title: Expanded Spell List
docs.text:
The following spells are added to the bard spell list for you:

Spell level Spells 0 Shape water 1 Create or destroy water 2 Wall of Water 3 Water Breathing 3 Water Walk 4 Control Water 4 Watery Sphere

Those spells don't count against the number of spells you know.

docs.title: Art of the Cascade
docs.text: At 3rd level, when you restore at least 2 hit points to a single target with a spell, the water orb can bounce to another target within 15 feet and restore half the original amount (rounded down). Art of the Cascade can trigger itself.

docs.title: Shield of Water
docs.text: At 6th level, while a creature has one of your bardic inspirations, it is surrounded by a thin sphere of water, granting it resistance to fire and acid damage and the ability to breathe underwater. When a creature consumes the bardic inspiration, the shield explodes. Creatures within 5 feet regain hit points equal to the number rolled on the bardic inspiration die. If a creature protected by your Shield of Water is healed by Art of the Cascade, a splash of healing water erupts, and all creatures within 5 feet regain hit points equal to your Charisma modifier.

docs.title: Inspired Cares
docs.text: At 14th level, when you use a healing spell, you can expend a bardic inspiration to restore the maximum possible number of hit points. This option can be used with multi-target features but affects only one target. You can use this feature during Art of the Cascade, and it affects the amount healed by the feature that triggered the cascade.

docs.title: Ranger : Star Thrower
docs.text: Rangers of this conclave read the night sky as both map and arsenal. By binding thrown weapons to a chosen constellation, they call down flashes of celestial power on their quarry and recall their star-marked arms with a gesture.

docs.title: Magical Constellation
docs.text:
By performing a 1-hour ritual, you can magically bind up to six weapons to a constellation. The weapons must have the thrown property. When you hit a creature with a ranged weapon attack using a bound weapon, the weapon attaches to the target, floating around it and following it. If the target is teleported or changes planes, the weapons detach and return to you. If a target has six bound weapons attached to it, it triggers the constellation's Star Fall, and the weapons return to you.

Constellation Name Star Fall Rose The target takes 2d10 radiant + 2d10 poison damage, and is charmed by you for a number of turns equal to your proficiency bonus Anvil The target takes 2d10 radiant + 2d10 force damage, and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become stunned for a number of turns equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) Claw The target takes 2d10 radiant + 2d10 necrotic damage, and is bleeding for a number of turns equal to your proficiency bonus Phoenix The target takes 2d10 radiant + 2d10 fire damage, and is burning for a number of turns equal to your proficiency bonus

docs.title: Shooting Star
docs.text: At 3rd level, when you take the Attack action and throw a bound weapon, you can use a bonus action to throw another bound weapon at the same target.

docs.title: Shiny Recall
docs.text: At 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can recall all your thrown weapons. For each recalled weapon that was attached to a creature, that creature takes radiant damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.

docs.title: Lucky Star
docs.text: At 7th level, when you miss with a thrown weapon attack using a bound weapon, you can still attach the weapon to the target. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus + 1. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

docs.title: Star Light
docs.text: At 11th level, when you hit a creature with a thrown weapon attack using a bound weapon, you deal additional damage equal to your Wisdom modifier. Moreover, when you trigger Star Fall: - the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become blinded until the end of its next turn; - you can expend a spell slot to add 1d10 radiant damage for each level of the slot.

docs.title: Light Speed
docs.text: At 15th level, using an action, you can throw all of your bound weapons at once (make separated attack rolls). Your walking speed is doubled and you don't trigger opportunity attacks until the end of your turn.

docs.title: Sorcerer : Thirsty blade bloodline
docs.text: It is said that these sorcerers placed a portion of their soul into their weapon. The blade answers its master's call, sharing in the power and the hunger that comes with their bond.

docs.title: Pact of the thirst
docs.text:
At 1st level, by performing a 1-hour ritual, you can bond a melee weapon to yourself. This weapon becomes your Thirsty Blade until you die or bond with another weapon. A Thirsty Blade can't receive any pact magic or be used for bladesong. The Thirsty Blade uses your Charisma modifier and gains the following benefits:

  • You are proficient with it.

  • Call of the Hunt. As a bonus action, you can teleport it to your hand and equip it. If your hand isn't free, the object in that hand is teleported to where the Thirsty Blade was.

  • Corrupted Blade. When you hit with it, you can spend 1 sorcery point to add a number of d6s equal to your proficiency bonus in necrotic damage.

  • Vampiric Feast. When you hit a non-construct creature with it, you regain a number of hit points equal to your Charisma modifier. If the attack kills the target, you regain 1 sorcery point and increase the healing by the excess damage dealt.

docs.title: Sorcerer's trick
docs.text: At 1st level, you can use your Metamagic on attacks made with your Thirsty Blade as though the blade were a 1st-level melee spell.

docs.title: Unstoppable thirst
docs.text: At 6th level, if you fall unconscious, your Thirsty Blade attacks on its own once per turn. It targets creatures within its reach, prioritizing enemies before other creatures and creatures with fewer hit points before those with more. These attacks use your Charisma modifier and proficiency bonus and trigger Vampiric Feast. The blade can't make opportunity attacks on its own.

docs.title: Great thirst
docs.text: At 14th level, your Thirsty Blade becomes more powerful. Corrupted Blade also prevents the target from being healed until the end of your next turn, and Vampiric Feast restores twice as many hit points.

docs.title: Thirsty Blade master
docs.text: At 18th level, your Thirsty Blade is a part of you, and attacking with it is so natural that you can cast a spell while attacking. After you make an attack with your Thirsty Blade, you can cast any spell that normally requires an action as a bonus action instead.

docs.title: Rogue : Underhand Blade
docs.text: Some people will do anything to win a fight. Rogues who follow the Underhand Blade know that honor is of no use to the dead.

docs.title: Cunning Tricks
docs.text:
You gain proficiency in the Deception skill. At 3rd level, you can use various tricks to gain an unfair advantage in combat. As a bonus action, you can use one of the following tricks:

  • Sand Toss. You throw sand in an enemy's face. The target must be within 5 feet of you, and you make an attack roll using Charisma. On a hit, the target takes 1d4 bludgeoning damage. It must also succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become blinded until the end of its next turn. You must have a free hand.

  • Disarm. You swing your blade and attempt to strike your enemy's weapon hand. Make a melee weapon attack. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 slashing damage. It must also succeed on a Strength saving throw or drop the weapon. If the target holds the weapon with two hands, it has advantage on the saving throw.

  • Leg Trip. You attempt to knock your enemy prone by striking its legs. The target must be within 5 feet of you, and you make an attack roll. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. The target must be your size or smaller.

  • Forbidden Strike. You attempt to strike your enemy in the abdomen or groin. The target must be within 5 feet of you, and you make an attack roll. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn.

  • Devious Mockery. You mock your opponent with total contempt. Cast vicious mockery. The saving throw DC for your Cunning Tricks equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

docs.title: Opportunistic
docs.text: At 3rd level, you have advantage on attack rolls against enemies affected by one of your Cunning Tricks.

docs.title: Honour is a Foreign Concept
docs.text: At 9th level, you master the art of deception in battle. When you take nonlethal damage, you can fake death and fall prone. While in this state, your next attack roll or opportunity attack has advantage, but it reveals your deception. Standing up uses movement normally. If you take nonlethal damage while faking death, you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + half the damage) or cry out and reveal your deception while remaining prone. An enemy won't fall for this trick twice and may try to kill you.

docs.title: Master of Deceit
docs.text: At 13th level, you know where to strike even heavily armored enemies. Your attacks ignore resistance to nonmagical slashing, piercing, and bludgeoning damage. You also gain expertise in Deception.

docs.title: Underhand Expert
docs.text: At 17th level, you double your Charisma modifier when calculating the DC of a Cunning Trick, and you add your Charisma modifier to damage dealt by a Cunning Trick.
